video_title: Mike Brown Joins Roommates: Road to NBA Finals, Reacting to Mikal's WILD IG Live & Career Evolution

quotes.speaker: Mike Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown on the importance of player buy-in for coaching success
quotes.excerpt: If you don't have buy-in from your players, you have no shot at coaching anybody else on the team.
quotes.quote: This is a players' league. If you don't have buy-in from your players, you have no shot at coaching anybody else on the team. And these guys made my job easy. I love Josh. You need a guy that wears his emotions on his sleeve, and he does do that. There were a few times I went to him and I said, 'Hey, I'm going to let you do what the hell you want. You do anything you want. Just play hard. I'm going to tell you what I'm thinking. If you don't like it, you have one opportunity right there, you can curse me out. I ain't going to say nothing back. But then after you curse me out, we got to end it. We got to try to work together to move forward.' And he was great with it.

quotes.speaker: Mike Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown on Tim Duncan's coaching philosophy and player-coach relationships
quotes.excerpt: If your best player doesn't allow you to coach him, you have no shot at coaching anybody else.
quotes.quote: I learned this during my time in San Antonio. I'll never forget at the end of my first year there, we were meeting as a staff, and Pop says, he's mumbling under his breath, he says, 'I got to thank Tim Duncan.' I said, 'You got to thank Tim Duncan? Why are you saying that?' And he said, 'Mikey, if your best player doesn't allow you to coach him, you have no shot at coaching anybody else on the team. And Tim allows me to do it.' And I will say that this man to my left allowed me to coach him, which allowed me to coach the rest of the team. Made my job easier. So, thank you both.

quotes.speaker: Mike Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown on the difficulty of bringing Josh Hart off the bench
quotes.excerpt: I came in with the idea of Josh coming off the bench. And I did it not because I don't think he's a starter.
quotes.quote: One of the lows was, and I'm not saying this just because you're sitting here, so I came in with the idea of Josh coming off the bench. And I did it not because I don't think he's a starter. I don't think you always start your quote-unquote best five players. You start five players and it's about who ends the game. But trying to find the different combinations throughout the course of the game was the part that I was looking at the most. And so, bringing Josh off the bench to start, and then us going through the struggles that we went through that early, because usually, in order to truly believe, it's good to have some success first and then to go backwards. But we almost started going backwards because of it to a certain degree, and then we had to bounce back from it.

quotes.speaker: Mike Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown on the challenges of managing player expectations and media distractions
quotes.excerpt: It got bigger than what it should have because the media started getting involved and others started getting involved.
quotes.quote: It got bigger than what it should have because the media started getting involved and others started getting involved. And I thought that was a distraction. And others started getting involved, and I thought, so I didn't know if we would recover from that. And I don't know if I'm going to recover from it with you, because I didn't know you that well. So, that definitely was a tough moment, dealing, you know, with the highs and lows with Kat, especially the first time, was pretty tough because, you know, again, you have a thought in your mind what you want to do, similar to bringing him off the bench, what you want to do offensively, what you want to do defensively, and to see what you envision not fit Kat, but you still think it could, was tough kind of going back and forth with him and trying to figure out what we needed to do.

quotes.speaker: Mike Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown on the importance of messaging and player accountability
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to add to the things that I believed in or that I thought would shape the culture.
quotes.quote: I wanted to add to the things that I believed in or that I thought would shape the culture of the group that would help us win. And that's the stuff that's our standard. I want guys that would be willing to sacrifice, who are trying to find a way to build that culture. I want competitive guys. I want guys that will help us stay connected, guys that would believe, not just in what we're trying to do, but believe in the process of what we're doing. And then at the end of the day, I wanted guys that would that would try to hold each other accountable. And if I gave the group of players ownership in the process, in due time, they would try to do all those things while also not being afraid to hold me accountable.
